novelty.reasoning: Core claims: (1) forced terseness causally increases per-token computation density; (2) this density gain saturates at a ceiling; (3) the ceiling predicts the accuracy cliff; (4) depth can be causally blocked/restored to test compensation. Closest prior work already establishes a depth-vs-length tradeoff and per-token density estimators, and latent-reasoning work shows depth can substitute for tokens in principle. The only real delta is the inference-time causal compression test and the predictive-ceiling framing, which is interesting but thin and close to an obvious next experiment rather than a clearly new phenomenon.
revision_notes: State the exact novel causal claim in one sentence and distinguish it from known depth-length tradeoffs; remove 'conservation' unless you formalize it.
Add a sharper related-work paragraph naming Think Deep, Not Just Long and explicitly explaining why your setting is not just a re-run of its depth/length redistribution result.
Narrow the claim to a measurable, falsifiable hypothesis about forced compression and compression-break thresholds, not a general theory of compute interchangeability.

impact.reasoning: Problem: understanding when shorter reasoning prompts preserve accuracy vs trigger failure, and whether there is a mechanistic limit to compression. Who cares: users and builders of reasoning LLMs, inference-time compression, and adaptive compute allocation. Downstream if true: can set safe compression limits, choose prompts/steering, and predict when terse reasoning will fail. Strongest case: a measurable ceiling on compensatory depth would give an actionable compression budget rather than a purely empirical token-accuracy curve.
revision_notes: Add a concrete user-facing use case: adaptive CoT shortening for latency/cost control with an accuracy safety bound.
Quantify the operational decision your method enables: 'compress until predicted ceiling, then stop' or similar.
Emphasize whether this changes deployment policy, not just mechanistic understanding.

review.reasoning: The proposal is testable, but the central hypothesis is loosely specified and heavily proxy-dependent. There is strong overlap with prior depth/length work, and several experiments risk being post-hoc correlations (raw vs matched tokens, logit-lens depth proxies, LLM-judge matching). The causal tests are plausible but need tighter controls and clearer falsifiability. Venue-readiness is limited by novelty risk and by insufficiently specified measurement validity.
